To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HCMV infection induces the mislocalization of IFI16 from the nucleus into the virus assembly compartment, where it is trapped in the virion.
HCMV mislocalizes the DNA sensor IF16 from the nucleus to the cytoplams and incorporates it into the virus assembly complex (VAC) where it is trapped within mature virions.
the innate immune sensor IFI16 binds HCMV DNA during the early stage infection and is entrapped in the egressing virions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the innate immune response to viral infection and its modulation by viruses to evade the immune system.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms by which HCMV subverts the innate immune response and how the virus exploits host cell machinery for its own benefit.
understanding how viruses manipulate cellular pathways to promote infection and replication, and how the innate immune system responds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IFI16 restriction factor, a constitutively expressed innate immune protein, is recruited into the cytoplasm during the early stage infection, is entrapped in the egressing human cytomegalviruses in vitro, and is mislocalized to late stage infection and is trapped within the human cytomegalvirus in vitro.

the HCMV protein kinase pUL97 interacts with the DNA sensor IF16, leading to its mislocalization to the cytoplamic virion assembly compartment, where it is incorporated into the virion, thereby escaping the host cell’s antiviral response.
IFI16 is an innate immune sensor of HCMV DNA that can restrict viral replication at the early phase of infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFI16 is an important restriction factor against HCMV infection.
HCMV is capable of manipulating IFI16 to its own advantage, and this manipulation is a key component of its immune evasion strategy.
IFI16 is a potent restriction factor against HCMV, and HCMV has developed mechanisms to evade IFI16 restriction by mislocalizing and trapping it within mature virus particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFI16 is an innate nuclear sensor and a restriction factor for HCMV replication and is entrapped in the egressing virus.
IFI16 is a bona fide innate immune sensor that restricts HCMV infection and that the virus has evolved mechanisms to evade this innate immune response by mislocalizing and trapping IFI16 in the AC.

IFI16 is a bona fide restriction factor that is mislocalized and trapped in the virus assembly complex during late-stage infection, thus providing a novel mechanism for the evasion of innate immunity.
